text: RCD10.5XES installation: the bottom-mounted compressor requires a lower intake vent so cool air passes over the compressor and electronics; the static condenser is fan-assisted. The upper exhaust vent may be in the RV roof. Keep 10-25 mm behind the cabinet and use the specified deflector or baffle. Overall dimensions are 1260 mm high, 550 mm wide and 615 mm deep. Recess dimensions are 1246-1251 mm high, 526-531 mm wide and 571-586 mm deep.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD internal venting requires an intake below the refrigerator and a clear exhaust path above it; performance may be slightly lower than external venting. The condenser is static but fan-assisted. Without an external lower service vent, the refrigerator must be removed to service the compressor, control module, DC adaptor or fan, so use at least a closable service hatch if limiting dust ingress. Internal vent kits: 9620017015 for RUC dual-hinge and 9620018441 for RUC/RCD.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD control panel modes. Performance mode uses automatic compressor speed, automatic outer fan and automatic defrost at cooling levels 1-5 and is the preferred general mode. Silent mode limits compressor speed, keeps the outer fan low, uses automatic defrost and levels 1-3; high ambient temperatures may cause long run times and reduced performance. Turbo uses high compressor and fan speed, disables defrost, selects coldest level 5 and runs for at most 12 hours before reverting. Avoid Turbo in very high ambient conditions if sub-zero plate temperature cannot be reached. Low Ambient Condition uses a 5 W heater below 12 C to prevent freezer warming while the fresh-food section waits to restart.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD Low Ambient Control heater operation: one temperature sensor in the refrigerator section controls the compressor, so in cold weather the freezer can warm while the refrigerator remains cold enough not to call for cooling. When the compressor cycles off and the LAC sensor detects ambient below 12 C, the 5 W heater switches on to warm the fresh-food evaporator and force an earlier compressor restart. The heater switches off when the compressor starts. This repeats until the sensor detects 15 C. The heater remains off during a refrigerator-stopping fault such as compressor low-voltage cut-out.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD warning and error alarms: solid warning means defective fresh-food sensor and sensor replacement is required. One flash means DC below 10 V or above 31.5 V; check wiring, connections, battery condition and connected solar, inverter or adaptor equipment. Two flashes means external-fan overcurrent; reset with the power button for 2 seconds and replace the fan if repeated. Three flashes means compressor will not start; check power interruptions, control module, refrigerant overcharge or locked rotor. Four flashes means compressor overload; reset, switch off 30 minutes and reduce load. Five flashes means compressor overheat; check ventilation and fan. Six flashes means CI-BUS fault and auto-resets. Seven flashes means door open more than 2 minutes and resets when closed.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD service cautions: do not drill into the cabinet sides or rear because vacuum-insulation panels may be punctured and warranty lost. Connect the condensate drain hose so water does not drip onto the fan or cause cabinet, electrical or fire damage. Use correctly sized pilot holes, screws and driver bits in the steel surround and do not over-torque. Check AC and DC fuses before replacing the main or display control board, and isolate AC power before removing covers.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: Qualified-technician compressor-control test for an RCD three-flash or compressor-not-starting fault: verify live DC power at the top two grey and red terminals; remove the orange wire from terminal C and blue wire from terminal T; bridge the C and T terminals briefly. If the compressor runs, the control module is likely serviceable. If it does not run with confirmed supply, check compressor windings for open circuit and replace the failed component as indicated. Also consider refrigerant overcharge, repeated power interruptions that prevent pressure equalisation, or a seized compressor.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page; qualified-technician warning added.

text: For the qualified-technician RCD compressor test, bridge the C and T terminals themselves after removing the wires; a separate wiring loop is unnecessary. Measure resistance across the three compressor pins: each pair should be approximately 2.7 ohms. An open circuit indicates a faulty compressor. Check that the control module is fully seated on the compressor pins and has not sprung away at the rear.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page; qualified-technician warning added.

text: RCD display-board access: the refrigerator doors do not normally need removal to access the display PCB and connectors, although door removal is required for frame-heater replacement. Carefully peel off the control decal for reuse. Release the clips at one end of the PCB mounting panel, push the panel into the cavity, rotate it and remove it diagonally through the opening. Connections include the LAC heater, frame heater and reed door switch. The automatic frame heater warms the freezer divider mullion to prevent condensation.
reviewNote: Visually checked against the rendered source page.

text: RCD operating data. Performance compressor speed by level: 1-2 = 2000 rpm, 3 = 2500 rpm, 4 = 3000 rpm, 5 = 3500 rpm; fan high. Silent levels 1-2 = 2000 rpm and level 3 = 2500 rpm with fan off. Turbo level 5 = 3500 rpm with fan high. Compressor-controller C-to-T voltage indicates speed: 0 V 2000 rpm, 1 V 2500 rpm, 2 V 3000 rpm, 3 V 3500 rpm. Battery positive fuse: 15 A at 12 V or 7.5 A at 24 V. Defrost follows 12 hours accumulated runtime, then forces operation for 60 minutes or until -1 C before a one-hour shutdown; power-off resets the 12-hour count. Temperature levels 1-5 cut in at 7, 5, 4, 3 and 2 C and cut out at 6, 4, 3, 2 and 1 C at the sensor.
